plan: [ This is a sealed-bid second-price auction with independent private values. The dominant strategy is to bid my true value because my bid affects only whether I win, not the price I pay (which is the second-highest bid). Overbidding risks winning and paying above my value in tie cases; underbidding risks losing when winning would be profitable. With no informative history and values redrawn each round, I will bid exactly my value to maximize expected profit. ]

[ This is a 3-bidder independent private-values second-price auction. With risk neutrality, the weakly dominant strategy is to bid truthfully: bid your private value. This maximizes expected profit regardless of others’ strategies and does not benefit from shading, especially with only 1 round and no exploitable history. Values are uniformly drawn and bids are in $0.1 increments; $44 is valid. If I win, I pay the second-highest bid, yielding expected positive surplus when my value is highest. ]

[ One-shot, independent private values, second-price auction with 3 bidders. With no history to exploit, the weakly dominant strategy is to bid my true value. Truthful bidding maximizes expected profit: underbidding risks losing when winning would be positive EV; overbidding risks winning when the second-highest bid exceeds my value, yielding negative profit. Tie-breaking does not justify overbidding, as it can force losses. Therefore, bid exactly my value, $29. ]
